title: Optimization of Laser Ablation Resistance for Multilayer Heterogeneous Thin Films Based on Optical–Thermal–Ablation Coupling and a BP Neural Network Surrogate Model
title_zh: 基于光热烧蚀耦合和BP神经网络代理模型的多层异质薄膜激光烧蚀抗性优化
summary: 多层异质薄膜在连续波激光加热下的热物理响应涉及由干涉引起的驻波吸收调制的不均匀体积发热，它控制着逐层相变序列和最终的热失效阈值——传统比尔-朗伯近似无法捕获的耦合。这项研究开发了一种光热烧蚀耦合模型，该模型可以解析驻波吸收曲线，并将其与具有潜热效应的温度相关瞬态热传导耦合，并在七个功率级别的激光损伤实验中进行了验证。构建了一个基于两阶段替代的框架来探索热物理设计空间，其中离散材料选择和连续层厚度共同控制吸收分布和熔化顺序。
abstract: The thermophysical response of multilayer heterogeneous thin films under continuous-wave laser heating involves non-uniform volumetric heat generation modulated by interference-induced standing-wave absorption, which governs the layer-by-layer phase-change sequence and the ultimate thermal failure threshold—a coupling that conventional Beer–Lambert approximations fail to capture. This study develops an optical–thermal–ablation coupled model that resolves the standing-wave absorption profile and couples it to temperature-dependent transient heat conduction with latent-heat effects, validated against laser-damage experiments at seven power levels. A two-stage surrogate-based framework is constructed to explore the thermophysical design space in which discrete material choices and continuous layer thicknesses jointly control the absorption distribution and melting sequence. The optimal architecture is identified as SUS304/Ag/Si₃N₄/SiO₂/ITO with a refined thickness profile of 21 µm/0.106 µm/0.18 µm/2.35 µm/0.05 µm under a 25 µm total constraint, yielding a 209.6 K reduction in peak temperature relative to the baseline. The analysis reveals three thermophysical mechanisms: (i) in the interference layer, the order-of-magnitude reduction in volumetric optical absorption dominates over the 2.5-fold difference in thermal conductivity in determining the peak temperature; (ii) the positive temperature coefficient of thermal conductivity in the SUS304 substrate provides a self-regulating thermal-sink effect; and (iii) the Ag layer exhibits a non-monotonic thermal response beyond its optical saturation thickness, governed by the competition between cross-plane thermal resistance and in-plane thermal spreading coupled with absorption-peak shifting. These results clarify how interference-modulated heat generation governs phase-change sequences and thermal failure in multilayer thin films.

title: Substantial Reduction of Hole Injection Barrier at the Au/Rubrene Organic Semiconductor Interface Using PFBT Self-Assembled Monolayers
title_zh: 使用PFBT自组装单层显著降低Au/肟并芘有机半导体界面的空穴注入势垒
summary: 使用自组装单层（SAM）进行表面官能化是一种有效且被广泛采用的策略，用于优化有机电子器件中的电荷注入和界面能量。特别是，2,3,4,5,6-五氟苯硫酚（PFBT）SAM被广泛用于提高金等贵金属电极的逸出功，并有利于有机半导体分子堆积的模板化。然而，对PFBT修饰的Au/有机半导体界面上厚度依赖性能级对准进行详细阐述的综合原位光谱研究仍然很少。
abstract: Surface functionalization using self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) is an effective and widely adopted strategy for optimizing the charge injection and interfacial energetics in organic electronic devices. In particular, 2,3,4,5,6-pentafluorothiophenol (PFBT) SAMs are widely employed to augment the work function of noble metal electrodes, such as Au, and favorably template organic semiconductor molecular packing. However, comprehensive in situ spectroscopic investigations detailing the thickness-dependent energy-level alignment across the PFBT-modified Au/organic semiconductor interface remain scarce. This study investigates the interfacial electronic structures of 5,6,11,12-tetraphenylnaphthacene (rubrene) deposited on air-exposed Au (Air-Au), ultraviolet-ozone-treated Au (UVO-Au), and UVO-Au-functionalized PFBT (UVO-Au/PFBT) using in situ X-ray and ultraviolet photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS and UPS). High-resolution XPS reveals that UV–O3 pre-activation forms an ultrathin gold oxide (AuOx) layer, thereby dramatically enhancing the chemisorption kinetics and packing density of the PFBT SAM. While UV–O3 treatment alone increases the work function of Au from 4.78 to 5.06 eV, subsequent PFBT chemisorption further elevates it to 5.33 eV via a pronounced permanent dipole moment directed toward the substrate. Consequently, the hole injection barrier at the Au/rubrene interface is progressively reduced from 0.65 eV for Air-Au to 0.40 eV for UVO-Au and ultimately down to 0.27 eV for UVO-Au/PFBT. This dramatic reduction reaches the thermodynamic Fermi-level pinning regime, providing direct spectroscopic evidence for establishing near-Ohmic contacts. These findings offer fundamental insights into contact-resistance minimization and interface design for high-performance organic optoelectronic devices.
